assessments.reasoning: §9.5.3 paragraphs 1, 8 and 12–13 describe the simple-call context, issuance, immediate selection of an open entry, and the closed-entry queue rule. Paragraph 21 expressly raises Tasking_Error if the called task completes or becomes abnormal before accepting a simple call. Paragraph 7 also propagates Program_Error to current protected-object callers if an entry-barrier evaluation raises an exception. A simple call may enter the queue after a closed check and face one of these later conditions. Paragraph 20 describes cancellation as a specific mechanism, and the text reviewed does not establish that each exceptional ending constitutes selection or cancellation under that mechanism.

challenge.method: Traced immediate selection, the ordinary closed-entry path, selection and abort cancellation, and an initially queued call whose target later completes or becomes abnormal. Read the surrounding §9.5.3 paragraphs 7 and 19–21 and consulted §§9.3 and 9.8 for task completion and abort terminology.
challenge.results: The baseline queue rule and the ordinary selection/cancellation paths are directly supported. The candidate condition permits later task completion before acceptance. The manual expressly raises Tasking_Error for that case and also describes Program_Error on protected barrier exceptions. The only-two-endings wording remains insufficiently bounded without addressing the exceptional paths.

limitations: This is an adverse specification reading. No local GNAT compiler or Ada front end was available to run a supplemental example.
The scope could be reassessed for the ordinary queuing rule with the exceptional paths expressly accounted for.
